sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: What type of energy do we get directly from the light and heat of the sun?
Which famous monument in Agra is renowned worldwide for its beautiful white marble architecture?
What is the process of twisting cotton fibers together to make strong yarn called?
Which natural movement of the Earth causes the change of seasons?
options: C) The pull of the Moon

questions.question_text: Which gas is primarily absorbed by trees from the atmosphere to make their food?
In the manufacturing of clothes, what machine is used to weave yarn into fabric?
Which of these is a non-renewable source of energy that we extract from the earth?
What do we call the outer solid surface layer of Earth where plants grow and animals live?
In the natural rhythms of nature, during which season do many trees shed their leaves?
Why is protecting the Earth's environment crucial for our future?
options: B) To ensure survival of all living beings
D) To dry up all rivers
questions.answer: B) To ensure survival of all living beings

questions.question_text: What is solar energy and how is it useful to us in daily life? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Solar energy is the light and heat we get from the sun. It is useful for growing plants, drying clothes, and generating clean, renewable electricity.

questions.question_text: Briefly explain the weaving process involved in making clothes. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Weaving is the process where two sets of yarn are crossed together tightly on a machine called a loom to create large pieces of fabric.

questions.question_text: Why is preserving historical monuments and unique places important for our country? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Preserving historical monuments is important because they tell us about our rich cultural history, showcase ancient architecture, and attract tourists from around the world.

questions.question_text: How do animals adapt to survive the cold winter season? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Many animals adapt to cold winters by growing thick fur coats, storing body fat, migrating to warmer places, or going into a deep sleep called hibernation.

questions.question_text: Name two simple ways students can reduce waste at home or school to protect the Earth. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Students can reduce waste by writing on both sides of their notebook paper and carrying a reusable water bottle instead of buying single-use plastic bottles.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are visiting a textile factory. Describe the journey of cotton from a fluffy ball to a finished shirt. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: First, the fluffy cotton bolls are cleaned and spun into strong yarn. Next, large weaving machines weave the yarn into rolls of fabric. Finally, the fabric is dyed in bright colors, cut into pieces, and carefully stitched into a beautiful finished shirt.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are standing at a famous historical monument. Describe what the architecture looks like and how it makes you feel. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I am standing before the magnificent Taj Mahal. The smooth white marble shines brightly under the clear blue sky, and beautiful gardens surround it. Seeing such grand ancient architecture makes me feel deeply amazed and incredibly proud of our cultural heritage.

questions.question_text: Explain how the rhythms of nature, like the monsoon season, affect the lives and daily actions of farmers in India. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The monsoon season brings heavy rainfall which is absolutely essential for agriculture in India. Farmers eagerly wait for these rains to sow their crops like rice and sugarcane. A good monsoon ensures a rich harvest, providing food for the nation and a steady income for farming communities throughout the year.

questions.question_text: Describe actionable steps a local community can take to protect 'Earth Our Shared Home' from the harmful effects of deforestation. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: A community can fight deforestation by organizing local tree-planting drives and ensuring the newly planted saplings are watered daily. They should promote the recycling of paper to reduce the demand for wood pulp, and educate children about the importance of forests in providing oxygen and homes for diverse wildlife.
